physical.summary: Man's cloth (Asante kente) formed of 21 narrow strips of  hand-woven imported rayon and cotton, hand-sewn together selvedge to selvedge. The warp is the same in all the strips: a base of purple cotton with yellow stripes running through it; three yellow stripes have also been introduced into the weft. Both ends of the cloth have complex weft-faced matching patterns, and the warp ends have been left loose to form a fringe. Across the face of the central area of the cloth have been introduced regularly-spaced weft blocks arranged to give a chequerboard alternation with the warp pattern. The weft blocks themselves are made of white, green, red and yellow rayon yarn, with varied discontinuous supplementary weft patterns introduced between flanking solid blocks of colour.

physical.title: cloth
physical.summary: Man's cloth (Ewe kente) composed of 19 strips of imported cotton, hand-woven and hand sewn together along the selvedges. The warp design is the same in all the strips, and is of blue cotton edged with narrow lines of yellow and white. The design is formed in the weft, and differs from one strip to the next, although the basic pattern is a chequerboard. The outermost strips on both sides have white lines against blue in both warp and weft. The adjacent inner ones are more elaborate but still only linear, while the 15 strips along the centre alternate weft blocks, of various colours and patterning, with figurative motifs, mainly of stools, diamonds and combs, in supplementary discontinuous weft set against the blue background. These peter out towards the ends where they are replaced by weft coloured lines. The cloth is hemmed by hand-sewing.

physical.title: cloth
physical.summary: Man's cloth (Kente) consisting of 21 narrow strips of cotton, plus a narrow edging strip of yellow, black and grey, along the bottom; it is hand-woven from imported European thread, and hand-sewn together along the selvedges. The complex warp pattern is identical in the 21 strips, and is built up from narrow stripes of white, black, red, and yellow cotton. The 'kente' pattern is provided in the weft which is arranged in such a way as to form a sort of chequerboard, with alternate strips containing either two or three blocks of pattern; in addition, paired lines of yellow cotton are regularly placed along each strip. The pattern blocks are all formed in the same way, using a second pair of heddles to gather the threads and obliterate the warp pattern, and are composed of three ground weft blocks of white, red, yellow, orange, black and grey thread. These frame two warp-faced areas in which are woven motifs in supplementary discontinuous yellow mercerised cotton (sometimes referred to as 'silk'). Many of these motifs show chickens pecking at the ground, others are of sheep, hour-glasses or are of purely abstract patterns. The warp ends have been hemmed with a line of hand-stitching.

There are six different warp designs on the strips (one of them being the oyokoman design); these are repeated over each half of the cloth but in a different order. The weft designs are equally varied: there is no standard pattern wither for the pairs of end blocks, or for the supplementary patterns between them. The warp ends have been left as a fringe.

physical.title: garment; cloth
physical.summary: Kente cloth, a rectangular man’s wrapper composed of 22 hand-woven narrow strips of imported European cotton, hand-sewn together along the selvedges. The strips are designed and assembled alternately to form a chequerboard pattern; both ends have a variant design that serves as a border to the main field. All the strips have the same base design with a warp of white cotton with a wide red stripe running along the centre, and a weft with alternating thin lines of black and white cotton. A pattern is created in the weft with double-blocks of lines of red, yellow, green and black rayon (using a second pair of heddles) that frame geometrically shaped patterns created by discontinuous supplementary weft in the same range of colours but in cotton, not rayon. The warp ends have been left as a fringe.

physical.title: cloth
physical.summary: Cloth (Ewe kente); two unrelated strips of hand-woven cotton hand-sewn together. One strip has narrow warp stripes of black, yellow, green, sand-coloured, white and red cotton with supplementary weft float patterns in red, yellow and white cotton. The other strip has broad green and white warp stripes separated by narrow red, black, white and yellow cotton stripes with supplementary weft float patterns and stripes in red, white, yellow, black, green and pink cotton. The hems have been hand-stitched at both ends.

physical.title: cloth
physical.summary: A single strip of hand-woven cotton (Asante kente) made from cotton and rayon. The warp is of stripes of dark blue and white cotton; the weft is of dark blue cotton, in some areas variegated with white. Over this ground weave are supplementary weft float patterns arranged in bands: these include red and yellow bars, and red, yellow and green zigzags, lozenges and stepped forms. The warp ends have been left as a fringe.

physical.title: cloth
physical.summary: Kente cloth, a rectangular man’s wrapper composed of 25 hand-woven narrow strips of European imported cotton and rayon, hand-sewn together along the selvedges. The strips are designed and assembled alternately to form a chequerboard pattern; both ends have a variant design that serves as a border to the main field. All the strips have a uniform warp design with a ground of with two wide stripes of red, green and yellow and two wide stripes of white cotton; the weft is of white cotton. The weft has six pairs of rectangular blocks of supplementary lines of varying colour (using a second pair of heddles) that frame geometrically shaped patterns formed of discontinuous lines of supplementary weft. These weft designs are in green, yellow, red, blue and black rayon. The design of these blocks varies in alternating strips: one strip has two blocks and three areas of discontinuous thread, while the next has three blocks and two areas of discontinuous thread. The warp ends have not been hemmed.

physical.title: cloth
physical.summary: Kente cloth, a rectangular man's garment, hand-woven in blue and white imported cotton, composed of 28 hand-woven narrow strips hand-sewn together along the selvedges. The 28 strips are made up of eight different patterns, which repeat regularly three times, and then irregularly for the last four strips. Five of the patterns are purely warp-faced; the other three have modifications introduced by variations in the weft. The warp ends have been hemmed by hand sewing.
